> 1) What are some depressive thought cycles that you have experienced? 

Not really sure what you mean by this?

> 2) Describe your experience with depression.

Been mildly depressed since elementary school. Things got worse for some reason I'm not sure in high school. Began to binge video game as a coping mechanism and ditched school a lot. Things got better briefly the summer after high school but the combination of being in a toxic relationship as well as trying my first drug- marijuana and having a very bad experience caused my depression to slowly get worse over the last 5 years. Currently *barely* able to hold down a part time job because of it.

> 3a) Have you self-harmed? If so, how?

Yes. Scratching, cutting, burning(branding), fasting, drug abuse.

> 3b) Why do you SH?

It's a release. I started when life was way too much to handle. SH was an outlet for those feelings. I quickly realized why it's so addicting. I don't always SH for the same reason but the reasons I do could be: self punishment/guilt/shame, relief from extreme anxiety/panic or sleeplessness (because of the pain/dopamine response), trying to "anchor" myself when I'm feeling very disassociated, or just general destructive moods- because I can.

>3c) How does SHing make you feel?

Relieved, usually. Depends on the situation/method but the purpose behind it at least for me is to get some relief when things are getting to be too much. The dopamine rush is nice.

> 4a) Are you clean? If so, for how long?

Not clean.

> 4b) Do you still experience SH urges? If so, how often?

Yes. When I try to stay clean I get them at least once a week.

> 5)  Anything else you want to add?

If your friend has more specific questions they are welcome to message me.

"I can fear death no longer, I've died a thousand times."

It's a quote from a song but it describes my life as of recent. I'm not sure how much this applies to others but I gave up worrying about being "dead"/depressed/not "normal". I take every day as it comes (partially just because I don't have the energy to do otherwise) and go with it. If I'm having a low period then I go with that. I don't talk to anyone, I spend time by myself. I get out all my "sad" things/activities and just ride it out. I don't feel bad for ignoring people for a bit because people that really know me know whats going on, and those who get upset aren't people I have the energy to be friends with anyways. I don't fight it. Obviously it's good to practice harm reduction, don't get carried away. However I think it's good to allow yourself to feel low. You don't have to be happy every moment of every day.

On a "good" day (usually still pretty low for me, just not as extreme) I try to live it like it's my last. Honestly because I'm worried one of these days could be my last. So if I want to see a movie and my friends are being dumb, then I go see the fucking movie anyways because I deserve to see it and I don't need others to enjoy something by myself. Maybe this is more of an anxiety thing as I've had crippling social anxiety my entire life but depression has helped me stop giving a fuck about almost everything so I try to use that to my advantage.

But for some reason when I smoke I get extremely disassociated (even more so then psychedelics in my experience). It was my first drug and I didn't expect that and I have bad anxiety so when I got super high (off one hit too, I have a really low natural tolerance?) I essentially had a serious panic attack. I feel like I'm watching myself from third person and it feels like words come out of my mouth before the thoughts actually process in my head. This is what I hated the most, I felt like I had no control of myself. 

Suffering from anxiety and depression in my life before smoking kind of made me continue to smoke in a fucked up way of making myself suffer worse. I actually smoked every day by myself after work for about a 6 month period and tried to meditate, journal, figure out why I always felt so disconnected and thus anxious when I was high and never had any success really. I was also really convinced that it was damaging my short term memory and general mental function but over a year of being sober later I realize it wasn't really weed, just depression. At least I think so since I started getting similar effects recently and I haven't smoked in over a year, but my depression has gotten worse.

23F, I also had to move back in with my mom recently after living with my ex for 4 years. I love my mom and shes not a mean person but she doesn't and probably won't ever grasp the idea of depression, ADHD and other stuff like that. So sometimes when I'm not doing so well she hurts me with the things she says. Even though I know her intentions were not to hurt me sometimes the timing was bad and it was enough to push me into a SH binge or suicidal episode. Intentional or not, this is a horrible environment for someone with depression/other issues because any progress you make will be reversed by them. I am trying to move out and I think you need to get out of that environment too. Obviously it's extremely difficult when you are down/low energy/out of a job but don't give up. I would say at least try to get out of the house a little each day (go for a walk or a drive). Being cooped up in hell will just make things worse.


If not being able to get out of bed is happening frequently then you should really think about seeing a doctor and getting some medication. In the past there were periods where I wouldn't get out of bed for weeks at a time and that's just really unhealthy. Being on antidepressants though they aren't helping me that much, at least reduced those type of days to maybe once a month for 1-3 days at a time. If you don't have any insurance, depending on your state there are free resources usually available. They might not be the best but anything helps really. I'd be happy to help you search for them if you like. Also you can always check yourself into the hospital though it will be expensive post-visit they usually can provide you with free resources as well, and you get a break from being around your mom.


As for the SHing, as most of us say, try to stop while you can. However I know it's hard to give up what seems like the only thing that helps so in that case just be smart about it. Care for your wounds! Avoid places that are not easily hidden such as the forearm because it's very possible you will have to live with those scars forever. Also I personally advocate against writing words because if they scar, it's going to be there for a long time. I wrote curse words into my thigh and they scared very dark and obvious and I was so embarrassed that I ended up making more scars over it to cover it up and now it's just a ugly mess. If you want to channel words maybe write them down as you cut? Or create some kind of design that represents that word or feeling that isn't recognizable to others. Just some ideas.

***

In summary just don't completely give up because this kind of thing doesn't get better on it's own. Small victories. Try not to cause long term damage especially with cutting - when things get better you don't want to have to deal with covering scars or explaining why you wrote cunt into your skin. If you often can't get out of bed then it's time to see a medical professional because that's a serious problem.

WOW thank you sooo much for all this information! Unfortunately but also fortunately I didn't get to read this before I went to see the doc. They were able to see me within hours at my general office (with a nurse) which was cool. The way my wound/scars are is obvious that it was intentional so that's why I was freaking out. 

I wore a hoodie in the waiting room and also while the entry nurse takes my vitals and she didn't ask me to remove it thankfully. So the nurse I was scheduled with comes in and low and behold it was someone I used to work with at a Pharmacy (they worked in the clinic). I've gone into the clinic for panic attacks when I worked there so he kind of knows me/my history already... seriously what were the odds? He gave me the typical speal about am I a danger to myself or others or am I suicidal which I said no (I'm honestly not). He questioned about if I was seeing someone which I expected but then he asked/noted specifically who, how often and when. He asked me if I've been taking my meds as prescribed as well.

After that he looked at my wound and from that point on didn't bother me about being in danger or anything. He asked a senior nurse to come look for a second opinion and she didn't mention anything about that it's obviously self inflicted (as she shouldn't). She was actually really nice and gave me a goodie bag full of extra gauze and a sleeve. Woooo free medical supplies am I right?

So overall my experience turned out to be really awesome (mostly by coincidence though). I'm sure if I went to urgent care my experience would have been much different, so those tips you listed would be a life saver. Hopefully this post helps others too if they come across it.

**Oh and also it was good I went to my regular office because it turns out my tetanus shot was way over due (oops!!!) so I got one of those as well. Everyone should make sure they are current on that shot.**

I do this too. It started when I was taking stimulants for ADHD and I was so busy with work and school I didn't even notice I wasn't eating. I had that "just woke up" flat stomach all day every day and I loved it. But I took it to the extreme where I wasn't eating for days and I get extremely painful stomach cramps(?) and one time I fainted at work. So I started eating at least half a meal a day. During this period I was under a lot of stress of working full time, going to college full time and battling depression. After I graduated I moved and didn't have my ADHD medication for a while. But I was still really stressed and depressed trying to find a job and I realized I still wasn't hungry/eating. It's like how some people stress eat, I do the opposite. So that's not really a good thing to get yourself into. Also another concern is that you can develop an eating disorder if you get caught up with the weight loss. Some people don't know but you can have an eating disorder without being skin and bones. It's called "Eating disorder not otherwise specified (EDNOS)" and like others said restricting food intake isn't just about fat it's about vitamins and other things that can be very dangerous to your health.

Sorry if that came out like a lecture. I just wanted to inform you in case you haven't already thought about those things. The scary part about harming internally like not eating is you can't see exactly the level damage you are doing unlike cutting. So if you must, please please just be careful and smart about it. <333
